summary: A 42-foot all-steel live-in lookout built in 1958 on Okanogan National Forest land; privately owned since 1996 and damaged by a 2015 fire, but still standing.

facts.status_note: Standing but damaged. Floorboards caught fire in the 2015 North Star Fire, bottom stairs were removed, and the tower has been privately owned since 1996 with no funded removal.
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Okanogan National Forest (tower privately owned)

access.note: Privately owned tower on national forest land. The bottom stairs were removed for visitor safety. No source says the tower is open to climbing.

visit.trail_note: Forest roads reach near the summit. WTA says a high-clearance vehicle can get within about 300 yards. TrailChick reports driving right below the tower in 2018. The lower stairs are gone.

events.note: Forest Service says it has not been used regularly since 1971 (quoted by NHLR)
Purchased by a private party and slated for removal; no removal funding exists
North Star Fire burned the surrounding area in September; embers reached the cab and caught floorboards on fire. Bottom stairs later removed for visitor safety (undated)
Registered April 11, 2022 as US 1524, WA 73; nominated by Christine Estrada

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 5,062 ft (1,543 m), firelookout.com gives 5088', WTA gives a 5,088-foot highest point, and TrailChick gives 5,096'. The record keeps the NHLR figure, which matches the brief's elevation_m of 1542.9.
NHLR names the Okanogan National Forest. TrailChick names the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The story uses the NHLR name.

notes_for_editor: Height 42 ft converted to 12.8 m. Brief elevation matches NHLR; other sources differ by about 30 to 35 ft. Current status is from TrailChick (updated March 2024) and firelookout.com ('as of last report', undated). Ramblr (2019) and geocache pages were not read. The stair removal is undated. Access is drawn from WTA and TrailChick; the story does not encourage climbing. No corrections to the brief.
